title: DS scope: what the language is for
preamble:
# DS scope: what the language is for

The domain DS serves, the patterns it makes first-class, and
the things it deliberately doesn't try to do. Everything else
in the spec is in service of this scope.

DS is a language with Rete-based semantics. The language spec
is abstract: it specifies what DS does rather than how a
runtime implements it, so integrators have a fixed contract to
write rules against. Two official runtimes implement it, libds
and the Mercury runtime, and they move in lockstep.

**DS is not a general-purpose production-system language.**
It makes first-class a narrow slice of Rete-based pattern
matching, extends it with orchestration primitives the domain
needs, and deliberately omits the rest. This doc is where
that cut is drawn.

## What this is not

- Not a feature list. Features live in the per-topic specs.
- Not a performance benchmark. Sizing below is design target,
  not measured result.
- Not marketing. This is an engineering scope — it exists to
  say no to features, not to sell the language.
